newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRODEUR GETS SEVENTH SHUTOUT AS DEVILS BLANK RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRODEUR GETS SEVENTH SHUTOUT AS DEVILS BLANK RANGERS.

text.p: Martin Brodeur turned back 26 shots to record his seventh shutout of the season Thursday as the New Jersey Devils blanked the New York Rangers 4-0 to move within two points of Philadelphia for the to spot in the Eastern Conference.
Bill Guerin and Scott Niedermayer scored powerplay goals in the first period to provide Brodeur with more than enough offence en route to his 18th career shutout.

Brodeur surrendered a soft go-ahead goal in the third period against Philadelphia Tuesday and blamed himself for losing the key matchup. He made no mistakes Thursday and his seventh shutout tied him with Colorado's Patrick Roy and Phoenix's Nikolai Khabibulin for the league lead.
"This was a different type of game. We started real strong and stayed that way the rest of the game," Brodeur said.
"It gives us confidence that we can play our style in a big game," Brodeur said. "If we want to make a big run at Philly, we have to win these games."
Steve Thomas extended New Jersey's lead to 3-0 just under four minutes into the third period and Bob Carpenter completed the scoring with a short-handed empty-net goal with 2:33 left.
"There are not many teams that can play with a 2-0 lead like New Jersey," said New York coach Colin Campbell. "They did a pretty good job of keeping us at bay."
In Boston, Robert Reichel had two goals and three assists to lead the New York Islanders to a 6-3 win over the Bruins.
Reichel, acquired from Calgary last week, set up a pair of tallies by linemate Zigmund Palffy 1:44 apart in the second period as the Islanders kept their playoff hopes alive.

The Bruins carried a 3-2 lead into the second period, but Reichel's second goal of the game tied it at 8:35. Palffy put the Isles ahead for good with 6:21 left in the period with his 40th of the season.
Tommy Salo made 38 saves and Travis Green and Bryan Smolinksi also scored for the Islanders. Jean Yves-Roy, Anson Carter and Tim Sweeney tallied for Boston, which suffered its fifth straight loss.
At Florida, Tom Chorske scored short-handed in the first period and added an insurance tally in the third and Steve Duchesne had a goal and an assist as the Ottawa Senators edged the Panthers 3-2.

Ron Tugnutt held the Panthers scoreless over the first two periods before losing his shutout bid on Rhett Warrener's goal with 2:12 left in the third. David Nemirovsky scored a powerplay tally with two seconds left for the final margin.
Tugnutt finished with 19 saves as Ottawa moved into a tie with Tampa Bay and the Islanders, three points behind Washington for the final East playoff spot.

At Tampa Bay, Steven Rice scored twice in a three-goal first period and Sean Burke turned aside 40 shots as the Hartford Whalers snapped a six-game losing streak with a 5-2 victory over the Lightning.

Andrew Cassels scored 24 seconds after Rice's second goal for a 3-0 Hartford advantage and the Whalers got third-period insurance tallies from Keith Primeau and Kevin Dineen one day after the team announced they would leave Hartford at the end of the season.
The win pushed the Whalers into ninth place in the East, two points behind Washington in the tight chase for the final playoff spot.
In St Louis, Joe Murphy and Geoff Courtnall each notched his 16th goal in the second period and Grant Fuhr made 29 saves to lead the Blues to a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings.
Brett Hull set up both goals for the Blues, who vaulted into a sixth-place tie with Anaheim in the West playoff race.

The Kings outshot St Louis 16-4 in the third period but Fuhr turned aside 15 shots in the period, maintaining the Blues' one-goal lead. Vitali Yachmenev had spoiled Fuhr's shutout bid one minute into the third with his 10th goal of the season.

In Phoenix, Gerald Diduck and Darby Hendrickson exchanged first-period tallies before goaltenders Nikolai Khabibulin and Felix Potvin took over as the Coyotes and Toronto Maple Leafs battled to a 1-1 tie.
Diduck gave Phoenix a 1-0 lead with a powerplay goal 5:35 into the game. Hendrickson answered for Toronto with an unassisted goal at the 13:12 mark.
Khabibulin turned aside 33 Toronto shots, while Potvin made 24 saves for the Leafs.
The tie moved Phoenix into sole possession of fourth place in the Western Conference.
